unit_note: All values in USD trillions unless stated. Canadian figures converted at market rates; CAD-native values kept alongside.

series.label: United States nominal GDP
series.note: Advance estimate. BEA revises twice; expect movement of a few tenths of a percent.

series.label: Canada nominal GDP
series.note: IMF full-year 2026 figure at market exchange rates. A separate Wikipedia compilation gives 2.42T for the same year, so treat the first two significant figures as solid and the third as soft. Currency conversion is doing real work here — a 5% CAD move changes this more than a year of growth does.
series.disputed: The World Bank puts Canadian nominal GDP at $2.32T for 2025 (FRED MKTGDPCAA646NWDB) against this IMF-basis $2.51T for 2026. Part of the gap is the year, part is the exchange-rate assumption. Treat the first two significant figures as solid.

series.label: Canada GDP per capita
series.note: Population 40.5M (IMF basis); StatCan puts Q2 2026 population at 41.4M, which would lower this.

series.label: US economy as a multiple of Canada's
series.source: Derived from the two series above
series.note: Derived. Kept here so the page never recomputes a ratio silently.

fx_cad_usd.note: US dollars per Canadian dollar. Lifted out of the page script, where it was a bare constant, because currency conversion does real work here: a 5 percent move in the Canadian dollar shifts the Canada bars more than a year of real growth does. Every converted figure on the page states the rate that produced it.
fx_cad_usd.inverse_note: DEXCAUS is published as Canadian dollars per US dollar.
